item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.11), AMZN Neutral (+0.13)] BCE data-centre expansion could reshape long-term growth, Desjardins says
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Neutral (+0.11), AMZN Neutral (+0.13)
BCE Inc. plans to significantly expand its Saskatchewan data-centre capacity to 1.2 gigawatts, a move that Desjardins Capital Markets believes could add substantial long-term value to the company. Desjardins maintained its Buy rating and C$41 price target, estimating the expansion could eventually contribute C$9 per share in value and materially alter BCE's growth profile. The project, which requires over C$5 billion in investment, is contingent on customer commitments and regulatory approvals, but is seen as a shift towards higher-growth infrastructure for Canada's largest telecom operator.

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.34), AMZN Bullish (+0.35)] Salesforce deepens its integrations with AWS and Google Cloud to support AI agents
item.description:

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.29)] Dyna Software Brings Enhanced Compliance Governance to ServiceNow Teams with Source Control Management (SCM)
item.description:

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.33)] Should you buy the SOX pullback? Citi weighs in

item.title: [NVDA Neutral (-0.10)] AI Stocks Fell, but Workday and Adobe Jumped. A Favorite AI Disruption Trade Just Flinched
item.description:

This shift suggests that established software platforms might have more time to integrate AI as a feature, rather than being disrupted by new AI models. Both companies showed strong AI adoption in their recent earnings reports, although long-term growth and market skepticism remain factors.

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.22)] Trump's Marijuana Rescheduling Push Is Back in Focus. Is Tilray Stock Finally a Buy?
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Bullish (+0.22)
The article discusses the renewed focus on President Trump's push to reschedule marijuana to Schedule III, a move that could significantly impact companies like Tilray Brands (NASDAQ: TLRY). While rescheduling wouldn't federally legalize recreational cannabis, it would ease research and expand medical marijuana opportunities, areas where Tilray already has a strong international presence. The author suggests that Tilray's improved financial standing makes it a more compelling investment now, even if broader federal reform faces further delays or never fully materializes.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.41)] Apple expands iCloud+ to include Apple TV and Apple Arcade in Mozambique
item.description:

item.title: [NVDA Neutral (+0.12), TSM Neutral (+0.13)] What Is Taiwan’s “Silicon Shield”—and Does It Still Protect Taiwan in 2026?
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Neutral (+0.12), TSM Neutral (+0.13)
Taiwan's "silicon shield," which posits that the world's reliance on its advanced semiconductors deters conflict, faces new scrutiny in 2026. While TSMC's global expansion and Taiwan's evolving AI hardware ecosystem reinforce its technological indispensability, vulnerabilities like energy security and food supply suggest the shield is not impenetrable. The article concludes that the silicon shield is best understood as economic leverage, requiring Taiwan to strengthen resilience and international partnerships to remain effective.

item.title: [NVDA Bearish (-0.23)] "Hoax": Nvidia CEO Puts Trump on Phone While Downplaying Dangers Of AI
item.description:

The event occurred as US tech stocks, including Nvidia, experienced a slump due to concerns about spending deceleration.

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.00)] Big Tech Issued About $220 Billion of Bonds. Alphabet and Meta Show How AI Is Warping the Credit Market
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Neutral (+0.00)
Big Tech companies like Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle have issued approximately $220 billion in bonds over the past year to fund data center expansion for AI. This massive bond issuance is starting to distort the credit market, even for high-quality borrowers, as investors demand more compensation for duration and supply. While this isn't a solvency warning for companies like Alphabet and Meta, it serves as a price signal, making financing more expensive and raising the bar for returns on AI investments.

item.title: [AAPL Bearish (-0.40)] Maryland Appeals Google, Apple, Peacock’s Take Down of Ad Tax
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bearish (-0.40)

The tax court had ruled that the tax unconstitutionally discriminates against large out-of-state companies like Google, Peacock TV, and Apple, and is preempted by the federal Internet Tax Freedom Act. This ruling could influence similar digital economy taxes in other states.

This new Siri leverages large language models for personalized searches of local data and general queries, with Apple emphasizing its "personal intelligence" and integration into its ecosystem. While it uses smaller, on-device models, more complex tasks will utilize Private Cloud Compute powered by Google Cloud infrastructure.

item.title: [MSFT Bearish (-0.26)] Amazon and Microsoft Can Buy GPUs. But U.S. Construction Is Short 439,000 Workers
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bearish (-0.26)
The U.S. construction industry is facing a significant labor shortage of 439,000 workers, creating a bottleneck for the AI buildout despite major investments from companies like Amazon and Microsoft. While these tech giants can finance large AI campuses and secure GPUs, they struggle to find skilled labor such as electricians and welders. This shortage leads to project delays, increased costs, and impacts the ability to quickly bring new data centers online and convert demand into revenue.

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.11)] Oracle begins new round of AI-driven layoffs: report
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Neutral (+0.11)
Oracle has reportedly initiated a new round of layoffs, impacting an estimated 3,000 to 4,000 employees. These job cuts are believed to be part of the company's strategy to reduce payroll costs and finance its significant investments in AI infrastructure buildout. This marks another substantial reduction in Oracle's workforce, following 21,000 job cuts earlier this year, as the company restructures around its AI adoption plans.

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.10)] AI CEOs call for slowing AI boom as billions flow to data centers
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Neutral (+0.10)
Leaders of major AI companies like Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI are advocating for a slowdown in frontier AI development, citing concerns over safety and the industry's ability to test and contain increasingly capable systems. This call comes despite massive investments in computing infrastructure, raising questions about potential timing and workload mismatches for data centers and power producers. The proposal emphasizes independent evaluation and coordinated safety standards to allow safeguards to catch up with rapid AI advancements.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.31)] Microsoft AI Safety Rules Send 3 Cyber Stocks Higher - Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), Palo Alto Networks (NASDA
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.31)
Microsoft's new AI safety framework, the "Humanist AI Code of Conduct," has led to a significant surge in three cybersecurity stocks: CrowdStrike Holdings, Palo Alto Networks, and Cloudflare. The framework emphasizes human control over AI systems, requiring them to stay within authorized boundaries and avoid independent goals. Investors are viewing these cybersecurity firms as crucial for providing the security infrastructure needed to manage increasingly autonomous AI.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.30)] Klarna props up new Apple phones
item.description:

Klarna has entered into a new device leasing program with Apple, financing the tech giant's latest and most expensive iPhones, including a $1,999 foldable model. This partnership marks Apple's first foray into a subscription model for hardware and allows consumers to lease devices for 12 or 24 months with options to upgrade, purchase, or return them. The move is seen as an incentive to drive more frequent device upgrades and help Klarna attract new users.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.14), MSFT Neutral (-0.13)] Musk’s xAI and X Corp. settle antitrust case against Apple
item.description:

Elon Musk's xAI and X Corp. have settled an antitrust lawsuit against Apple Inc., agreeing to dismiss the case. The lawsuit, filed in August, accused Apple of favoring OpenAI's ChatGPT over competing chatbot makers and sought billions in damages. While the settlement with Apple is finalized, claims against OpenAI for alleged monopolistic practices in the chatbot market remain active.

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.02)] US judge says she will stay on OpenAI case after divesting Microsoft stock
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Neutral (+0.02)
U.S. Magistrate Judge Ona Wang has decided to remain on a landmark copyright lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft after divesting her Microsoft stock. Wang, who is overseeing pretrial issues, stated that judicial rules would typically require recusal but that her divestment negates the conflict and her continued involvement is in the public interest. The lawsuit, brought by authors and news outlets including The New York Times, alleges that OpenAI and Microsoft used copyrighted material to train ChatGPT without permission.

item.title: [AAPL Bearish (-0.26)] Apple apparently doesn’t want you hanging out at its stores anymore
item.description:

Apple is reportedly planning a major revamp of its retail stores under new CEO John Ternus, shifting focus from community gathering places to more traditional retail spaces. This change will involve bringing back dedicated Genius Bars, removing large video walls, and redesigning "Avenue" sections for online order collection and "Today at Apple" workshops. The strategy aims to prioritize sales over community connection, with stricter rules also being implemented for employees.

item.description:

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.13)] Chip stocks down: AMD, Nvidia, Intel, and Sandisk lead market selloff after AI bosses call for a pause
item.description:

Shares of major semiconductor companies like AMD, Intel, TSMC, and Nvidia fell after AI leaders, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, OpenAI's Sam Altman, and Microsoft's Satya Nadella, called for a slowdown in AI development due to safety concerns. These leaders fear AI could reach a point of "recursive self-improvement" making it difficult for humans to control. The market selloff reflects investor reaction to these warnings.

This move comes after a significant 91% year-to-date surge for GLW, driven by strong AI infrastructure demand, hyperscaler deals, and an Nvidia-backed expansion. item.title: [TSM Bullish (+0.43)] Taiwan Semiconductor September Revenue Surges 53% and Can’t Keep Up With Demand
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bullish (+0.43)
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) reported a 53% year-over-year surge in August 2026 revenue, reaching $16.35 billion, significantly exceeding its own full-year guidance. Despite this strong financial performance, TSMC is struggling to meet customer demand, particularly due to tight packaging capacity and a significant gap between demand and supply for AI chips. The company is aggressively expanding its capacity, with 20 fabs under construction, and anticipates continued strong demand from the AI sector through 2029-2030.

item.title: [TSM Bullish (+0.83)] World’s largest contract chipmaker TSMC sees August revenue surge over 53% to record high
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bullish (+0.83)
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) reported a record monthly revenue for August, surging over 53% year-on-year to $16.35 billion, primarily driven by robust demand for chips used in artificial intelligence applications. The company has maintained its dominant market share in the global foundry market, with strong bookings for its advanced chipmaking capacities. TSMC also announced a collaboration with ASML to advance next-generation chipmaking technology, planning to use ASML's High NA technology for advanced nodes starting in 2030.

item.title: [TSM Bullish (+0.18)] Intel Climbs 5% on High-NA EUV Production Lead, ASML and Taiwan Semiconductor Advance 3%
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bullish (+0.18)
Intel's stock surged 5% after the company announced a lithography milestone, processing over one million wafers on High-NA EUV equipment, including production layers for its Panther Lake processors, putting it years ahead of rivals like Samsung and TSMC in this advanced technology. ASML and Taiwan Semiconductor also saw gains of 3-4% due to AI-driven demand and Intel's achievement. Intel's Q2 revenue rose 25%, marking its strongest growth in over 15 years, though its significant year-to-date gain already reflects high investor optimism.

item.title: [TSM Bullish (+0.51)] ASML and TSMC Announce Initiative to Pioneer Industry Transition to Large-Format Photomasks for High NA EUV
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bullish (+0.51)
ASML and TSMC have announced a collaborative initiative to drive the semiconductor industry's transition to 12-inch photomasks for High NA EUV lithography. This move aims to increase fab productivity, lower chipmaking costs, and remove stitching constraints, enabling more cost-effective advanced chips. The initiative plans for a 12-inch mask pilot line by 2031, with full lithography system readiness for advanced node production by 2033.

item.title: [TSM Neutral (+0.02)] Why Taiwan’s Silicon Shield Is Failing
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Neutral (+0.02)
Taiwan's "silicon shield," stemming from its dominance in advanced semiconductor manufacturing, is facing challenges as China invests heavily in chip self-reliance, particularly in mature-node chips. While Taiwan still holds leverage in cutting-edge chips, China's increasing capacity in 28-nanometer chips threatens to make Taiwan's shield irrelevant for its own economy, potentially leading to a more fragile global trade environment with rising chip prices. This shift means that the geopolitical importance of Taiwan's chip production will no longer solely rely on the most advanced technologies, but also on the control of common chip manufacturing.

item.title: [TSM Neutral (+0.01)] Where Does AMD Make Its Processors?
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Neutral (+0.01)
AMD processors are primarily manufactured in Taiwan by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), the world's largest semiconductor producer. While TSMC has facilities in Arizona for some AI chips, the final assembly and packaging of AMD CPUs occur in places like Penang, Malaysia, and China. This manufacturing strategy is similar to Nvidia's, with TSMC also producing chips for other major tech companies like Apple and Tesla.

item.title: [TSM Bullish (+0.51)] Marvell Technology and Taiwan Semiconductor are No-Brainer Picks: They Have What Wins in a Gold Rush
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bullish (+0.51)
Marvell Technology (MRVL) and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) are presented as strong investment opportunities in the AI infrastructure buildout, likened to selling "picks and shovels" during a gold rush. Both companies reported impressive Q2 revenue growth (around 36%), with TSMC demonstrating broad market exposure through its foundry services and Marvell focusing on custom silicon and optical interconnects for hyperscalers. While TSMC offers a steadier investment due to its foundational role in chip manufacturing, Marvell, despite being higher-variance, shows significant growth potential, particularly with its custom silicon business projected to more than double by fiscal 2028.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) announced an additional $100 billion investment in its Arizona operations, bringing its total U.S. commitment to $265 billion. This expansion will fund four more semiconductor fabrication plants and advanced packaging facilities, solidifying Arizona's role as a key hub for advanced chip manufacturing. The investment aims to create tens of thousands of high-paying jobs and strengthen the U.S. semiconductor supply chain, driven by the surging demand for artificial intelligence.

item.title: [TSM Bullish (+0.47)] TSM Rides on AI, Advanced Nodes & Capacity Expansion: Worth a Buy?
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bullish (+0.47)
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM) is poised for continued growth driven by the surging demand for AI infrastructure, rapid adoption of advanced process technologies, and expanding global manufacturing capacity. The company reported strong Q2 2026 revenues and expects continued robust demand, especially with the industry's shift towards agentic AI. TSM's leadership in leading-edge nodes like 3nm and the upcoming 2nm and A16 technologies, coupled with international capacity expansions, are strengthening its competitive position and addressable market opportunities.
